verdict: Cisco's revenue jumped 18% to a record $17.3B as networking demand surged, lifting net income 51% to $3.9B even after a $511M restructuring charge.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +18% YoY, vs $14.7B a year ago — a record quarter

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: +52% YoY, vs $0.64 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $1.22

kpis.label: Networking revenue
kpis.note: +28% YoY — the core business and the growth engine this quarter

kpis.label: AI infrastructure orders
kpis.note: Orders from hyperscalers (the big cloud builders) in Q4 alone; $9.3B for the full fiscal year

segments.name: Networking
segments.note: Switches, routers and the gear that moves data — the core business. Up 28% as data-center and AI build-outs drove what Cisco calls a networking supercycle; networking product orders rose 40%.

segments.name: Security
segments.note: Software and services that protect networks and users. Up 14%.

segments.name: Collaboration
segments.note: Webex meetings, calling and contact-center tools. Up 12%.

segments.name: Observability
segments.note: Software that monitors apps and systems to spot problems early. Up 6% — the smallest product line.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Support, maintenance and consulting attached to the products. Flat vs a year ago at $3,793M.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building new products and features. Up 2% YoY, from $2,380M.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling products and supporting customers and partners. Up 5% YoY, from $2,818M.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Finance, legal and running the company. Down 4% YoY, from $706M.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of technology bought in past acquisitions over its useful life. Down from $254M a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Restructuring and other charges — costs of the restructuring plan announced in May 2026. Up from just $35M a year ago — see one-offs.

otherDetail: Interest and other income, net, added $669M: $822M of other income, net — mainly gains on investments — plus $220M of interest income, less $373M of interest expense.

takeaways.title: Record revenue, led by networking
takeaways.text: Revenue hit a record $17,252M, up 18%. Product revenue rose 24% while services were flat. Networking jumped 28% to $9,791M, Security rose 14%, Collaboration 12% and Observability 6%. Total product orders rose 35%, and AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers were $4B in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Profit grew much faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 38% to $4,264M, a 24.7% margin, and net income rose 51% to $3,859M, or $0.97 per diluted share. Interest and other income added a net $669M, helped by investment gains, and cash flow from operations was $5,386M, up 27%.

takeaways.title: A big restructuring charge sits in the costs
takeaways.text: Restructuring and other charges jumped to $511M from $35M a year ago under the plan announced on May 13, 2026, which Cisco expects to be substantially complete by the end of fiscal 2027. Total GAAP operating expenses rose 10% to $6,799M; leaving out restructuring, share-based pay and similar items, they rose 5%.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges were $511M in Q4, up from $35M a year ago, under the restructuring plan announced on May 13, 2026. Cisco excludes these charges from its non-GAAP results and expects the plan to be substantially complete by the end of fiscal 2027.

Other income, net of $822M was boosted by about $869M of gains on investments (before smaller offsetting losses) that Cisco also excludes from non-GAAP results. It is the main reason interest and other income swung to a $669M gain from an $88M loss a year ago.
footerNote: As reported in $M in the Q4 FY26 release; the lines tie exactly. The revenue split is the release's product groups plus Services.
